book: Sindh Textbook Board Physics Practical Journal, Class X, test edition
text_extraction: All 47 pages are scans with no extractable text; experiment and figure mappings were visually verified against rendered pages and installed target thumbnails.

calibration.scene_width_rule: raw XML width / 100, provisionally interpreting 10/15/18 as centimetres rather than metres
calibration.status: Nominal starting calibration; measure the actual printed target crop before claiming physical calibration.
calibration.pdf_bounds_note: Approximate visible diagram bounds are recorded in 1100-pixel-high page renders. They exclude surrounding page borders included in some tracking crops. The named enhanced/cleaned targets can have a different aspect ratio from the scanned diagram, so these bounds must not be treated as exact target crops.
calibration.pdf_scale_rule: At 100% printing, diagram width in metres = pixel-bounds width / render-pixel width * MediaBox width in points / 72 * 0.0254; Fit to page changes this scale.

source_corrections: Ohm's law text on printed page 16 contains an inverted R=I/V statement; use R=V/I.

Telescope apparatus on printed page 12 reverses objective and eyepiece focal-length roles. Follow the longer-focal-length objective and shorter-focal-length eyepiece shown in its procedure and diagram.
Microscope focal-length precautions on printed page 15 contradict each other; use physically consistent compound-microscope optics rather than those numeric statements.
Sample electrical observation tables contain inconsistent arithmetic. Demonstrations use explicit internally consistent example values, not purported measurements.

experiments.title: Refraction through a glass slab
steps: Outline the slab and mark the incident ray
Align pins to trace the refracted and emergent rays
Measure the incidence and refraction angles
Repeat and compare refractive index and lateral displacement

experiments.title: Refractive index of water using a concave mirror
steps: Place the horizontal mirror under a vertical needle
Remove parallax without water and record OC
Add a thin water layer and refocus to record OA
Repeat and calculate refractive index n = OC / OA

experiments.title: Critical angle and total internal reflection in glass
steps: Direct a narrow ray into the glass
Increase the internal angle of incidence
Observe grazing refraction followed by total internal reflection
Record the critical angle and repeat

experiments.title: Ray path and angle of deviation through a prism
steps: Outline the prism and place incident-ray pins
Align emergent-ray pins through the prism
Draw both normals and extend the incident and emergent rays
Measure deviation and repeat for other incidence angles

experiments.title: Convex-lens focal length by parallax
steps: Align the object pin, convex lens and search pin
Move the search pin to the inverted image
Remove parallax and measure object distance p and image distance q
Repeat and calculate f = p q / (p + q)

experiments.title: Astronomical telescope
steps: Align a long-focus objective with a distant object
Locate its real inverted image
Place a short-focus eyepiece near that image and focus
Compare angular sizes and calculate magnification fo / fe

experiments.title: Compound microscope
steps: Place a small object just beyond the objective focus
Locate the enlarged real inverted intermediate image
Align an eyepiece with the intermediate image inside its focus
Observe the enlarged virtual image and refine the focus

experiments.title: Ohm's law using a wire conductor
steps: Connect the source, key, rheostat and ammeter in series
Connect the voltmeter across the test wire
Close the key and vary current with the rheostat
Compare voltage and current; verify constant R = V / I

experiments.title: Resistors in series
steps: Connect two resistors and the ammeter in one series path
Connect the voltmeter across the resistors being measured
Close the key and record voltage and current
Compare individual and combined resistances: Rs = R1 + R2

experiments.title: Resistors in parallel
steps: Connect resistor branches across the same two source terminals
Measure the common branch voltage
Compare branch currents with the total source current
Verify I = I1 + I2 + I3 and reciprocal resistance addition

experiments.title: Galvanometer resistance by half deflection
steps: Connect a high resistance R in series with the galvanometer
Close the main key and note the initial deflection
Close the shunt path and adjust S to halve the deflection
Repeat and calculate galvanometer resistance G = R S / (R - S)

experiments.title: Magnetic field of a bar magnet
steps: Place the magnet on paper and trace its outline
Use a compass to mark the field direction near a pole
Move the compass along the marks and join the points
Repeat along other paths; outside lines run from north to south
